name: Sassafras

facts.what: Young leaves (filé); root bark for traditional tea
facts.how: Dry and grind leaves; steep root bark
facts.when: Leaves spring to fall; roots year-round
facts.where: East Texas woods and fence rows
facts.value: Flavor and tradition more than nutrition

caution: Root tea contains safrole, which the FDA flags in quantity; treat it as an occasional tradition, not a daily drink. The mitten-shaped leaves make ID easy.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: One tree, three leaf shapes on the same branch: oval, mitten, and three-lobed. Scratch a twig and it smells of root beer, because this is where root beer began.

sections.title: Filé
sections.body: Dry young leaves, grind, and sift: that is filé, the gumbo thickener. A single small tree supplies a kitchen for a year.
